messages.author: e3013c8b53cceacd
messages.subject: significance test between levels
parts:
Hi all, 

I have been using unmarked for a few months now and really enjoy the package. However, I work for someone who is less up to date on modern statistical methods. Being a newb myself, I find it difficult to offer clear explanation as to why I can or cannot do something he wants.

I have used the unmarkedFrameDS to analyze some line transect surveys via model selection and model averaging/relative importance values. I have results that tell the story appropriately, habitat type is the categorical covariate that we are most interested in and also shows up in all of the top models for density/abundance (there is also a continuous covariate for detection and another continuous covariate in the density function). There are four levels of habitat type and my task is to make a box plot and get p values for essentially pairwise differences. I think something like this is what I am after:


However, I cannot figure out how to get to this plot using unmarked. Using predcted values, I can make bar charts with confidence intervals/error bars and a line chart with the same over time (another effect that is in the top mode/high RIV). But I have not been able to figure out how to make exactly what he wants. 

Does anyone know of a a web page with instructions that uses unmarked? GGplot/pubr does not seem to work to well with the unmarked dataframe. 

I have also tried to use the TUKEY HSD, but ran into similar problems with the unmarked dataframe. Is there is something I can do with the predicted values that would get to the ?

At this point I think I have to make this outside of the unmarked package, which would not take into account distances. 

Any help/advice is appreciated.

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] significance test between levels
parts:
Hi Chance,

You can use linearComb to test pairwise differences among levels of a factor. You can’t use functions like TukeyHSD because those methods were developed for linear models.

Richard

messages.author: b5dd939eb0150bdb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] significance test between levels
parts:
Hey Chance,

I've run into a similar problem when using unmarked. I think there are a few pieces that are tripping you up here. The first is that you should give linearComb a vector of numbers not characters. Here's an example with some simulated data:

library(unmarked)
library(AHMbook)

# Generate some distance data using a function from AHMbook
sim_out <- simHDS("line", nsites=100, mean.sigma = 2, show.plot=F)

# Tidy things up so it works well enough with the format function
data <- data.frame(sim_out$data)
data$site <- factor(data$site, levels=as.character(seq(1,100,1) ) )

# Format the data for input into unmarked
yDat <- formatDistData(data, distCol = "d", transectNameCol = "site",
                       dist.breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.5))

# Make some fake habitat categories
habitat <- rep( c("A", "B", "C", "D"), each=25)

# Put this in a data frame
covs <- data.frame(hab=factor(habitat))

# Run things like Chance
umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat), siteCovs=covs,survey="line",

dist.breaks=seq(0, 3, 0.5), tlength=rep(3000, 100),
                       unitsIn="m")

hn_Hab.Ht2 <- distsamp(~1 ~hab, keyfun="halfnorm", umf)

Then you can use linearComb to figure out what the average abundance is in habitat A. You just put in a 1 for a covariate class you want included and a 0 for one you don't. The covariate order is the same as what's listed in the model output. You can wrap backTransform around this too like you were trying to do in your earlier code.

linearComb(hn_Hab.Ht2, coefficients = c(1, 0, 0, 0), type = 'state')

The post you referenced before was looking for a way to get those nice p-values for all combinations of covariates.

You could do something like this:

covs$hab <- factor(covs$hab, levels=c("B", "A", "C", "D"))
umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat), siteCovs=covs,survey="line",

dist.breaks=seq(0, 3, 0.5), tlength=rep(3000, 100),
                       unitsIn="m")

hn_Hab.Ht2 <- distsamp(~1 ~hab, keyfun="halfnorm", umf)

Where you change the order of factor levels so that you're contrasting abundance/density in A, C, and D habitats against B. You can also do the same with relevel but it looks a little uglier. Basically you're telling R to consider habitat "A" in the example below as the intercept, you can change it to whatever category you like.

hn_Hab.Ht2 <- distsamp(~1 ~relevel(hab, "A"), keyfun="halfnorm", umf)

Hopefully that helps some and hopefully I haven't given any spurious advice.

-Jerry

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] significance test between levels
parts:
Here’s another solution, to complement Jerry’s suggestions. This is for an N-mixture model, but the approach should be fairly generic. 

## Simulate data from model: y~Bin(N,p); N~Pois(lam) where 
## lam is function one factor with 3 levels

dat <- data.frame(x1=gl(3,30, labels=LETTERS[1:3]))
dat

nSites <- nrow(dat)

X <- model.matrix(~x1, dat) # design matrix
beta <- c(-1, 1, 2)         # coefficients of the log-linear model
lam <- exp(X %*% beta)      # expected value of abundance at each site

N <- rpois(nSites, lam)             # site-specific abundance
y <- matrix(rbinom(n*4, N, 0.5), n) # repeated count data

## Fit model in unmarked
library(unmarked)
umf <- unmarkedFramePCount(y=y, siteCovs=dat)

fm1 <- pcount(~1 ~x1, umf, K=100)
fm1

## Create dummy coefficients for each level of the factor. 
## These would need to be modified if there are other covariates in the model or if there are not 3 levels of the factor.
xA <- c(1, 0, 0)  
xB <- c(1, 1, 0)
xC <- c(1, 0, 1)

## Compare A vs B
## Test null hypothesis that mean abundance in level A is 
## equal to mean abundance in level B (on the log scale)
AvB <- linearComb(fm1, xA-xB, type="state")
AvB
confint(AvB)

## Compare A vs C
## Test null hypothesis that mean abundance in level A is 
## equal to mean abundance in level C (on the log scale)
AvC <- linearComb(fm1, xA-xC, type="state")
AvC
confint(AvC)

## Compare B vs C
## Test null hypothesis that mean abundance in level B is 
## equal to mean abundance in level C (on the log scale)
BvC <- linearComb(fm1, xB-xC, type="state")
BvC
confint(BvC)

I have results that tell the story appropriately, habitat type is the categorical covariate that we are most interested in and also shows up in all of the top models for density/abundance (there is also a continuous covariate for detection and another continuous covariate in the density function). There are four levels of habitat type and my task is to make a box plot and get p values for essentially pairwise differences. I think something like this is what I am after:


However, I cannot figure out how to get to this plot using unmarked. Using predcted values, I can make bar charts with confidence intervals/error bars and a line chart with the same over time (another effect that is in the top mode/high RIV). But I have not been able to figure out how to make exactly what he wants. 

Does anyone know of a a web page with instructions that uses unmarked? GGplot/pubr does not seem to work to well with the unmarked dataframe. 

I have also tried to use the TUKEY HSD, but ran into similar problems with the unmarked dataframe. Is there is something I can do with the predicted values that would get to the ?

At this point I think I have to make this outside of the unmarked package, which would not take into account distances. 

Any help/advice is appreciated.

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] significance test between levels
parts:
Is there a name for the pairwise comparisons above? 

For example in the literature I see pairwise comparisons like:

we used Tukey’s pairwise comparison
we used Tukey's honestly-significant-difference test to make pairwise comparisons
 I used Tukey's post-hoc two-way comparison tests
 Fisher's test of least significant difference (LSD) was used to make pairwise comparisons among treatments and nesting guilds

I realize those tests are for linear models as Richard said above, but it seems like there should be a more specific name for the test. Or should this be sufficient for a publication, "To investigate the effect of different habitat types, we tested the null hypotheses that predicted mean density in each habitat is equal using pairwise comparisons"?

On Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at 9:23:43 PM UTC-5, Jerry Cole wrote:
Thanks for the elegant solution Richard! That's way better than my hacked together code.

On Wednesday, February 20, 2019 at 6:08:50 PM UTC-8, Richard Chandler wrote:

Here’s another solution, to complement Jerry’s suggestions. This is for an N-mixture model, but the approach should be fairly generic. 

## Simulate data from model: y~Bin(N,p); N~Pois(lam) where 
## lam is function one factor with 3 levels

dat <- data.frame(x1=gl(3,30, labels=LETTERS[1:3]))
dat

nSites <- nrow(dat)

X <- model.matrix(~x1, dat) # design matrix
beta <- c(-1, 1, 2)         # coefficients of the log-linear model
lam <- exp(X %*% beta)      # expected value of abundance at each site

N <- rpois(nSites, lam)             # site-specific abundance
y <- matrix(rbinom(n*4, N, 0.5), n) # repeated count data

## Fit model in unmarked
library(unmarked)
umf <- unmarkedFramePCount(y=y, siteCovs=dat)

fm1 <- pcount(~1 ~x1, umf, K=100)
fm1

## Create dummy coefficients for each level of the factor. 
## These would need to be modified if there are other covariates in the model or if there are not 3 levels of the factor.
xA <- c(1, 0, 0)  
xB <- c(1, 1, 0)
xC <- c(1, 0, 1)

## Compare A vs B
## Test null hypothesis that mean abundance in level A is 
## equal to mean abundance in level B (on the log scale)
AvB <- linearComb(fm1, xA-xB, type="state")
AvB
confint(AvB)

## Compare A vs C
## Test null hypothesis that mean abundance in level A is 
## equal to mean abundance in level C (on the log scale)
AvC <- linearComb(fm1, xA-xC, type="state")
AvC
confint(AvC)

## Compare B vs C
## Test null hypothesis that mean abundance in level B is 
## equal to mean abundance in level C (on the log scale)
BvC <- linearComb(fm1, xB-xC, type="state")
BvC
confint(BvC)

On Wed, Feb 20, 2019 at 7:56 PM Jerry Cole <jsc3...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hey Chance,

I've run into a similar problem when using unmarked. I think there are a few pieces that are tripping you up here. The first is that you should give linearComb a vector of numbers not characters. Here's an example with some simulated data:

library(unmarked)
library(AHMbook)

# Generate some distance data using a function from AHMbook
sim_out <- simHDS("line", nsites=100, mean.sigma = 2, show.plot=F)

# Tidy things up so it works well enough with the format function
data <- data.frame(sim_out$data)
data$site <- factor(data$site, levels=as.character(seq(1,100,1) ) )

# Format the data for input into unmarked
yDat <- formatDistData(data, distCol = "d", transectNameCol = "site",
                       dist.breaks = seq(0, 3, 0.5))

# Make some fake habitat categories
habitat <- rep( c("A", "B", "C", "D"), each=25)

# Put this in a data frame
covs <- data.frame(hab=factor(habitat))

# Run things like Chance
umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat), siteCovs=covs,survey="line",
                       dist.breaks=seq(0, 3, 0.5), tlength=rep(3000, 100),
                       unitsIn="m")

hn_Hab.Ht2 <- distsamp(~1 ~hab, keyfun="halfnorm", umf)

Then you can use linearComb to figure out what the average abundance is in habitat A. You just put in a 1 for a covariate class you want included and a 0 for one you don't. The covariate order is the same as what's listed in the model output. You can wrap backTransform around this too like you were trying to do in your earlier code.

linearComb(hn_Hab.Ht2, coefficients = c(1, 0, 0, 0), type = 'state')

The post you referenced before was looking for a way to get those nice p-values for all combinations of covariates.

You could do something like this:

covs$hab <- factor(covs$hab, levels=c("B", "A", "C", "D"))


umf <- unmarkedFrameDS(y=as.matrix(yDat), siteCovs=covs,survey="line",
                       dist.breaks=seq(0, 3, 0.5), tlength=rep(3000, 100),
                       unitsIn="m")

hn_Hab.Ht2 <- distsamp(~1 ~hab, keyfun="halfnorm", umf)

Where you change the order of factor levels so that you're contrasting abundance/density in A, C, and D habitats against B. You can also do the same with relevel but it looks a little uglier. Basically you're telling R to consider habitat "A" in the example below as the intercept, you can change it to whatever category you like.

hn_Hab.Ht2 <- distsamp(~1 ~relevel(hab, "A"), keyfun="halfnorm", umf)

Hopefully that helps some and hopefully I haven't given any spurious advice.

-Jerry

I have been trying to find a solution for this, but cannot seem to get the linearcomb command to work for my model with a categorical covariate. I try it with only count variables and it works fine.

Example of code:

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : 
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘linearComb’ for signature ‘"unmarkedFitDS", "character"’

Not sure exactly what I need to do, but likely modify the language to specify all four types of habitat (A, B, C, D) so I can get pairwise comparisons? I found someone with a similar problem but never got an answer here: link.

On Sunday, February 3, 2019 at 9:39:21 AM UTC-5, Richard Chandler wrote:

Hi Chance,

You can use linearComb to test pairwise differences among levels of a factor. You can’t use functions like TukeyHSD because those methods were developed for linear models.

Richard
